title: South Korea's PIPC activates an emergency response and inspection support system for data breaches, with three months of intensive management
date_note: Etnews says the PIPC announced it on the 27th; the page gives no earlier day.
geo_basis: national agency, country as stated; pin at Seoul
summary: Etnews reports that South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission said on the 27th it is activating an emergency response and inspection support system to prevent and respond quickly to breaches. It will strengthen threat-information sharing with the Ministry of Science and ICT, the Financial Services Commission and the National Intelligence Service. Intensive management runs for three months from next month, per the article.
plain: Korea's privacy regulator says it is starting an emergency system to help prevent and respond to data breaches, with three months of intensive management starting next month, according to Etnews.
exec: Korean organisations face urgent inspections and stricter investigation of preventable breaches, according to Etnews' report of the PIPC announcement.

validation.note: Only Etnews was read; it quotes the PIPC announcement. The PIPC's own page was not read.

review.note: Compared title, 27 Nov date, agencies, three-month period against Etnews; single_source ok
